title: Singleton price cache captures a scoped DbContext and mutates a plain dictionary

consumerGuidance.architecture: ASP.NET Core Web API with EF Core; services registered in ServiceRegistration.cs.
consumerGuidance.notes: AppDbContext is registered scoped by AddDbContext. The API serves concurrent requests on Kestrel.

mustCite: the AddSingleton<PricingCache> registration alongside the scoped AppDbContext registration
the captured AppDbContext field in PricingCache
a concurrent caller reaching the singleton per request
the consequence that one request-scoped context is reused and disposed under other requests
a proportionate correction such as resolving the context per operation through a factory or scope
the unsynchronized Dictionary field on a singleton
a real interleaving of two concurrent requests writing the same key
the consequence of corrupted state or an InvalidOperationException during resize
a proportionate correction such as ConcurrentDictionary or a lock

forbiddenFindings.example: Requiring an IPricingCache interface because the class has none.
Objecting to the _entries field name or to var in GetOrAdd.
Reporting a dependency-inversion violation with no affected caller or consequence.

notes: Mirrors the guide's first calibration example. The scoped-in-singleton defect and the unsynchronized dictionary are separate findings on the same change.
